newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures closed higher but off their highs in low volume as investors turned cautious about the notionnel's ability to push much higher.
Most dealers and analysts still believe 132 on the March contract is attainable but added that goal depends on continued strength in the dollar and other U.S. markets.

The March future briefly touched 131.96, a new session high, after the release of market-friendly data on January U.S. retail sales. On Wednesday night, the contract went as high as 132.02 in after hours GLOBEX trading, before falling back.
Dealers said the market was quiet overall on Thursday and predicted it would probably be the same on Friday.
Analysts said the OECD's forecast that the French deficit to GDP ratio would be 3.2 percent in 1997 had no effect on markets.
Markets paid more attention to an announcement by the Bank of France that it decided to exempt repo transactions from reserve requirements.

The move will translate for banks into an increase of around one billion francs in their liquidity, the Bank said. It eases by 13 percent the amount of deposits that the banks must constitute to satisfy reserve requirement rules, it said.
The move, it said, was aimed at taking into account "the development and maturity of the French repo market to assure access in fully harmonious conditions to all economic players".
The Bank stressed, however, that the move was strictly confined to repo operations and did not put into question the role that reserves can play in carrying out monetary policy.

The central bank said the decision was aimed at allowing the repo market to develop fully against a European backdrop in which it will be among one of the most important intervention tools of the European central bank system.

Until now, repo operations with a maturity equal to or below one year carried out with credit establishments by resident counterparties were subject to reserve requirements. The exception was when those counterparties were themselves the credit etablishments subject to the reserve needs.
This constituted a differentiating factor among the various market players which it "seemed desirable to abolish", it said.
The Bank left its intervention rate unchanged at 3.10 percent after its Monetary Policy Council meeting, as expected.
The Treasury auctioned 595 million Ecus of 5.50 percent, 2007 OATs. The auction had a bid to cover ratio of 2.9.
